I've attached a diagram of my current system architecture. Can you identify any potential bottlenecks?

Looking at your architecture diagram, I can see several potential bottlenecks. The most significant is the single database instance handling both read and write traffic — at scale, you'll want to add read replicas and potentially a caching layer like Redis in front of frequently-read data.

The API gateway also appears to be a single point of failure. Consider adding a load balancer in front of multiple API gateway instances, with health checks and automatic failover.

What caching strategy would you recommend for this use case?

For your read-heavy workload, I'd recommend a cache-aside pattern with Redis. When a read request comes in, check the cache first. On a cache miss, read from the database, store the result in Redis with an appropriate TTL, then return the result. Invalidate cache entries on writes to the corresponding data.
